title: JK 018 sweet potato (LSU Purple): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: JK 018 sweet potato: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: JK 018 sweet potato is a sweet potato variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: JK 018 is a registered sweet potato variety, also sold or known as LSU Purple or NSIC Sp 25. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2002 as NSIC 2002 Sp 25. It comes from PhilRootcrops, Leyte State University (now VSU). Its record notes 11.68 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for LSU Purple or NSIC Sp 25, this is the same sweet potato. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [sweet potato variety finder](/crop-varieties/sweet-potato), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for root crops](/land-preparation/root-crop-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Its average yield of 11.68 t/ha trails the average of its group, 15.15. It sits in the lower quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in the registry trials, rated under natural field conditions
rows: Took some damage but held up

blocks.text: It was weak against weevil, so scout for it from the early weeks.

The pests and diseases that hit sweet potato fields most often: [root knot nematode](/diseases/root-knot-nematode). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its roots have purple flesh and cream skin. Dry matter is 36 percent. A higher dry matter cooks mealy and gives processors more flour or starch from each tonne. The starch content is 15.73 percent.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** 11.68 t/ha in registry trials, 8.32 t/ha in a 2025 Masbate college biofertilizer trial.
**Fruit:** Cream skin, purple flesh, long elliptic roots, dry matter about 36 percent.
**Uses:** Table, sweetpotato jam and other delicacies.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: one of the four improved varieties Central Luzon growers kept after on farm testing, a purple fleshed table and jam type. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant JK 018 sweet potato

The registry recommends it for anywhere in the country. Pick by use and market: yellow or orange flesh for snacks and fries, purple for processing, white for boiling. Weevils are the main enemy, so plant clean cuttings and harvest on time.

items.q: Is LSU Purple the same as JK 018?
items.a: Yes. LSU Purple is another name for JK 018, registered as NSIC 2002 Sp 25. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows 11.68 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
The registry recommends it for anywhere in the country. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of JK 018?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
